problems.description: Embeds a full async WebSocket subsystem (threading + asyncio + RLock) inside the monolithic sync Flask app.py, raising cognitive complexity by +9 and coupling two concurrency models in one module.
Module-level singleton `notification_server` holds mutable client state that leaks across test runs with no reset/isolation mechanism; test_health relies on fresh state.
test_notification_server.py reports a module-level constant naming violation (should be UPPER_CASE) per the mechanical scan.
No test coverage for websocket_handler's message parsing/disconnect path or the error/cleanup branch (finally-unregister).

strengths: _WebSocketAdapter cleanly isolates the websockets v10 `send` vs `send_text` API difference at the protocol boundary
Thread-safe client registry with RLock, and lock released before awaiting I/O (no held-lock deadlock)
Type-hinted public signatures on classes and methods per project convention
Solid unit tests using a FakeWebSocket covering broadcast, direct delivery, and health endpoint
SonarQube delta shows -2 smells and 0 new bugs, +179 lines entirely additive with zero duplications
commit_reviews.summary: Well-structured, well-tested greenfield addition of a notification server that improves code quality metrics, but it introduces moderate debt by mixing async/threading inside the monolithic app.py with an untestable module-level singleton; note one measured convention violation references transports.py, a file not present in this commit's diff.

problems.description: Module-level constants in test_notification_server.py should be UPPER_CASE per the convention report (one of the two flagged violations is introduced by this commit).
Channel validation/stripping logic is duplicated across subscribe, unsubscribe, and broadcast instead of being factored into a shared helper.
broadcast falls back to payload.get('channel') when the explicit channel arg is absent, creating an implicit coupling between message routing and payload shape that is easy to misread.
No test covers unregister cleanup of channel membership (that a disconnected client is removed from channels), the most leak-prone path.

strengths: New channel state is guarded by the existing _clients_lock, preserving the module's established thread-safety discipline.
broadcast signature extension is backward compatible via an optional channel param, so existing call sites are unaffected.
Empty channels are deleted after unsubscribe/unregister, preventing membership leaks.
Dynamic subscribe/unsubscribe over websockets follows the existing message_type dispatch pattern cleanly.
REST endpoints for channels mirror existing route conventions and provide observability.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped feature addition that slots cleanly into the existing lock-based architecture with backward compatibility, minor issues being duplicated channel-validation logic and one new uppercase-constant convention violation.

problems.description: RedisBroker methods silently swallow exceptions (hset/hdel/sadd/srem wrapped in bare except: pass), making broker-state divergence from the in-memory registry invisible to callers.
Dual state sources (Redis pub/sub + broker bookkeeping vs the in-memory clients/channels registry + SQLite messages table) with no reconciliation path if the broker drops a write.

Asymmetric error handling: remember_client/remember_subscription call connect() lazily while forget_client/forget_subscription check `self.client is not None`, so forgetting can silently no-op after a reconnect.
Fallback path pings Redis on every publish with 0.2s connect timeouts; under an unavailable broker this adds latency per message until the client is dropped.

Measurements flag module-level constants needing UPPER_CASE in test_notification_server.py and transports.py, but neither file appears in this diff's shown hunks, so these violations appear pre-existing rather than introduced here.

strengths: Clean optional-dependency pattern: guarded `import redis` with an unavailable-broker fallback keeps the app runnable without Redis.
Backward-compatible extension: DATABASE retained as an alias of DATABASE_URL, and NotificationServer gains a broker via constructor default without breaking callers.
Message envelope extended with optional channel/recipient/origin fields without altering the existing broadcast shape.
Broker wiring sits at the correct seam (register/unregister/subscribe/unsubscribe), preserving the RLock thread-safety model.
Zero new bugs, zero duplication, small delta (+274/-15) for a session-scoped integration step.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped integration commit that threads a Redis pub/sub broker and message persistence through the notification server with clean fallback semantics and backward compatibility, marred only by quiet failure swallowing and a mild dual-source-of-truth smell.

problems.description: Module-level constants should be UPPER_CASE in transports.py (and test_notification_server.py) per the measured convention violations. Note: test_notification_server.py is not in this diff, so its violation appears pre-existing.

websocket_handler duck-types transport.handle_connection via getattr with a runtime RuntimeError fallback, but handle_connection is not part of the BaseTransport ABC contract, leaving the seam inconsistent with the declared abstract boundary.

TRANSPORT env-var selection currently supports only one implementation (WebSocketTransport), which is a mild over-abstraction for one concrete transport — acceptable as an extension seam, not yet justified by a second backend.

strengths: Extracts a clean protocol boundary (BaseTransport/WebSocketTransport) decoupling NotificationServer from websockets, confirmed by measured -35 cognitive complexity and -2 smells with 0 new bugs
Removes duplication by consolidating the _WebSocketAdapter and per-client send/failure handling into the transport layer
Graceful failure handling: failed broadcasts/direct sends trigger client unregistration, preserving prior semantics
Good docstrings and type hints consistent with project conventions; new transport module is well-organized with an ABC interface
commit_reviews.summary: A solid, debt-reducing refactor that cleanly decouples the notification server from its WebSocket transport behind a well-defined ABC, with the only discrepancies being the minor measured convention violations (one in a test file untouched by this commit) and a slightly inconsistent getattr-based seam for the connection handler.

problems.description: Uses datetime.utcnow(), which is deprecated in Python 3.12 and removed in 3.13; prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc) for the cleanup cutoff.
The /history `since` filter compares ISO timestamps as raw strings; format drift (e.g. microseconds present vs absent) yields wrong boundary results. Tests don't cover the since path.
Server allow_message() detects broker capability via hasattr() duck-typing rather than an explicit interface; works but is a fragile seam.

Measurement flags module-level constants should be UPPER_CASE in test_notification_server.py; note transports.py (also flagged) is not touched by this diff, so that violation is pre-existing and not attributable to this commit.
Cognitive complexity +35 concentrated in message_history's nested branch/validation logic; early-return validation would flatten it.

strengths: Rate limiting is placed on the Redis broker seam, keeping Redis as the distributed source of truth while returning None (allowed) when Redis is unavailable to preserve local operation
Deployable configuration via env vars read at use time with safe fallbacks for invalid values
/history reuses the extracted _message_rows helper, removing payload-parsing duplication that previously existed inline
Cleanup background task lifecycle is symmetric with start/stop (created on start, cancelled and awaited on stop)
New tests cover the rate-limit behavior including message-not-dropped semantics
No new dependencies beyond stdlib timedelta; bugs +0 and smells -2 confirm no regressions
commit_reviews.summary: Adds rate limiting, message TTL cleanup, and a /history endpoint that fit cleanly onto existing broker/get_db/route seams with tests and no dependency or bug regressions, though the timestamp-string filtering and utcnow usage are minor maintenance risks.

compounding_issues: Seed bug persisted: create_task() inserts status='done' but returns status='pending' — a latent data bug surviving all 5 sessions, undetected because no test exercises task status

Module-level global singleton notification_server = NotificationServer() instantiates a RedisBroker at import time, creating import side effects and test-order coupling (test_health asserts 0 clients on the shared singleton)
Dual client registry: NotificationServer.clients and transport.clients both track the same connections and must be kept in sync manually
Redis broker asymmetry: remember_* methods call connect() to lazily reconnect but forget_* methods no-op when self.client is None, so subscription/client cleanup can silently fail to reach Redis
Binary churn in VCS: __pycache__/*.pyc and todos.db are committed from Session 3 onward, bloating every subsequent commit (sessions 3, 4, 5 all touch binaries)
Sync sqlite get_db() calls (_persist_message, _cleanup_messages) run inside the asyncio event loop, blocking it
key_decisions: Session 1 introduced a _WebSocketAdapter seam to isolate the websockets 10.x library API, which later enabled clean extraction of the transport layer
Session 3 added an optional Redis pub/sub broker with graceful unavailable fallback (returns None / False when Redis is down), decoupling local vs distributed delivery
Session 4 extracted an abstract BaseTransport boundary into transports.py, making NotificationServer transport-independent (env-driven via TRANSPORT)
Session 5 implemented rate limiting as a fixed one-minute Redis counter inside the broker, failing open when Redis is unavailable
Session 5 added SQLite message persistence (messages table) plus a TTL-based background cleanup task and a /history endpoint
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically across the five sessions, with no regression. Test count grew cleanly 3 → 6 → 8 → 8 → 10 passing tests, and the architecture matured from a single-file async/threaded server (Session 1) to a channel/subscription model (Session 2), then gained Redis pub/sub integration (Session 3), a transport abstraction (Session 4), and cross-cutting concerns of rate limiting, retention, and history (Session 5). Session 3 showed the one genuine stumble — an intermediate 3-failed/5-passed pytest run — but the agent self-corrected to 8 passing, demonstrating recovery rather than degradation. Session 4 shrank app.py by 90 lines while keeping tests green, and Session 5 built directly on the broker and transport seams from Sessions 3-4. The main persistent wart is the untouched seed bug in create_task and the growing binary churn in version control.
story_review.summary: A coherent greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc that builds naturally at each step, with quality improving across all five sessions via recovered test failures and steadily cleaner architecture, held back only by an untouched seed bug and committed build artifacts.
